newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDISH DEBT FIRMS IN STRONG MARKET DESPITE CROWN.
newsitem.headline: SWEDISH DEBT FIRMS IN STRONG MARKET DESPITE CROWN.

text.p: Swedish long debt yields inched down a touch in the early session despite a softer crown.
The 10-year bond yield slid one basis point to 6.54 percent while the six month T-bill rate was flat at 4.38 percent.
"The market has underlying strength. There are people buying debt papers on the curve and outright," a dealer said.
The focus was Swedish second quarter Gross Domestic Product due at 1100 GMT. GDP was seen rising 0.7 percent for a year-on-year rise of 2.1 percent.
The mark firmed to 4.3025 against the crown from 4.2910 late on Wednesday in jittery trade.
One dealer said a U.S. bank had sold crowns.

"It helps that the dollar is losing strength. So far it's been very speculative, it's a nervous market, which spills over to the crown," a dealer said, adding the crown could weaken to as much as 4.3250 against the mark.
